content:
Apple has released the first iOS 27.2 developer beta for iPhone. This update comes right after iOS 27 was officially released to all users on Monday. It also skips iOS 27.1, which Apple has been showcasing as a version focused on iPhone Duo.

iOS 27.2 beta 1 launches ahead of iOS 27.1 beta

This beta release comes right after the official launch of iOS 27 on September 14. The new version is a large update weighing in at 22GB.

Apple has detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK will let developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see here how apps appear on iPhone Duo depending on which iOS version they target.

But this release of iOS 27.2 developer beta 1 currently skips iOS 27.1.

Apple appears to want to hold back iPhone Duo-specific code until closer to the new hardware launch in October. However, developers still need to prepare their apps for the new device. Apple says the relevant tools are expected to be ready by the end of September.

Apple has also previewed other changes coming to all iPhones next month. These include a redesigned Apple Health app and expanded Siri AI support.

Apple confirmed this week: "Siri AI is now available in beta, offering a more capable and conversationally fluid assistant experience, with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, on-screen awareness, and more system-level app actions, currently available in English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish support to be added in October."

This likely gives us an early idea of when the official version might be released.

Once we've actually run this first version, we'll have a clearer picture of what Apple has included.

We'll have a separate highlight piece later covering the new features and other changes in this new beta update. Please stay tuned to our continuously updated iOS 27.2 beta coverage.
